The lever here is to push HIGHER, not just clear baseline. Design-doc hint (solver_dual_ddomain_bilateral_n2i.md 'Hints for the next autoresearch agent'): the projection-domain stack is in the symmetry trap on phantoms (proj sigmas near-identity -> stacked proj BFs stay locked-symmetric, proj_n_bf increase = wasted params), so spend the parameter budget on the IMAGE side. The image-domain stack 'readily differentiates into a multi-scale cascade (BF1 mild + tight sigma_r, BF2 wider, BF3 widest)'. img_n_bf 1->3 grows the image denoiser from 3 to 9 trainable scalars (total network 6->12 params, still ultra-low) for a genuine multi-scale image-domain cascade. Held fixed: proj_n_bf=1 (no point stacking the near-identity proj filter), kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), all six sigma inits (proj 1.0/2.0/0.02, img 1.5/1.5/0.02), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 (-> identical val split, directly comparable to iter-1). Wall: iter-1 ran 126 s; adding 2 image-domain BFs per FBP roughly 2-3x the per-step image cost but image-domain is a tiny fraction of the 128-view FBP+proj cost, so well under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard. Hypothesis: a 3-deep image-domain bilateral cascade gives the denoiser multi-scale capacity (coarse smoothing + edge-preserving fine pass) that a single image BF cannot, lifting val_score above iter-1's 0.6657 without the proj-stack symmetry waste -- and without enough parameters to memorise (12 scalars). If it does NOT move val_score, that confirms the image-domain BF is also near its structural ceiling on this dense phantom substrate and the next iter should pivot to img kernel/sigma tuning instead of depth.

PIVOT from DEPTH to RANGE-SIGMA TUNING, because depth is now in clear diminishing returns and PSNR has SATURATED. Trajectory: iter-1 img_n_bf=1 val 0.6657/hr+0.2763/PSNR 19.47; iter-2 img_n_bf=3 val 0.7465/hr+0.3276/PSNR 20.10 (+0.081 SSIM, +0.63 dB); iter-3 img_n_bf=5 val 0.7705/hr+0.3335/PSNR 20.18 (+0.024 SSIM, only +0.08 dB). The SSIM deltas are halving each depth step (+0.081 -> +0.024) and PSNR has flatlined (20.10 -> 20.18) -> img_n_bf depth has hit its structural ceiling; one more notch (5->7) would buy <0.012 SSIM at best. The higher-EV move is to make the deep 5-layer cascade we ALREADY have actually edge-preserving. Per docs/runs/mayo_campaign_state.md 'N2I PER-IMAGE knob insights' (confirmed cross-run 2026-06-18/19): on breast/demo (128-view substrates) the IMAGE-domain over-smoothing lever is img_sr, and 'default 0.02 too loose -> degenerates to a Gaussian blur ... Tighten img_sr->0.0005 for edge preservation'. The whole 5-deep cascade currently initialises every layer's RANGE sigma at 0.02, so each of the 5 BFs starts in the loose-Gaussian regime that smooths across phantom edges -> caps SSIM. Tightening img_sr to 0.0005 makes all 5 layers edge-preserving from init (sigma_r << data range preserves edges; sigma_r >> range degenerates to Gaussian, per solver_dual_ddomain_bilateral_n2i.md). This maximally leverages the deep cascade (5 layers x tighter range) and targets exactly the SSIM-capping over-smoothing rather than the exhausted PSNR/noise axis. Chose img_sr over img_n_bf 5->7 (exhausted lever, flat PSNR) and over img_kernel (a less-informed guess: kernel sets spatial extent, but the symptom here is range-domain over-smoothing across edges, which img_sr governs directly). Held fixed: img_n_bf=5, proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), proj sigmas (1.0/2.0/0.02), img spatial sigmas (img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 (-> identical val split, directly comparable to iter-1/2/3). Wall: iter-3 ran 235 s; img_sr is an init value, zero added compute, so wall ~unchanged, comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and 1200 s outer_wall_s guard. Hypothesis: tightening the image-domain range sigma to 0.0005 stops the 5-deep cascade from degenerating into a Gaussian blur across phantom edges, preserving fine structural detail and lifting val_score above iter-3's 0.7705 (the SSIM/edge axis, which still has headroom, not the saturated PSNR/noise axis). If it does NOT move val_score (or regresses), it confirms the image-domain BF range sigma is already effectively tight after training on this substrate and the next iter should pivot to img_kernel (spatial extent) or img spatial sigmas.
